packet.headline_seed: Top Zambian opposition figures arrested days after presidential vote

The leading opposition candidate in last Thursday's presidential election, Brian Mundubile, was also found at the scene of the raid in the capital, Lusaka, according to the country's top civil servant Patrick Kangwa. In an interview with the BBC, Mundubile dismissed the accusations as "total fabrications", saying security forces staged an assassination attempt on his life during a raid at his home on Friday. With results from more than half of the constituencies announced, he is trailing incumbent Hakainde Hichilema. Mundubile had earlier claimed victory and alleged there were voting irregularities.
The leading opposition candidate calls allegations of a planned insurrection as "total fabrications".

Giving details about the raid, Kangwa said the individuals arrested were connected to "military plans involving foreign nationals and illegal military training camps". He added that they posed "a serious threat to state security" and held "high-grade military weapons", ammunition and other materials intended for use in an armed insurrection. He alleged that shots were fired at law enforcement officers leading to an exchange of fire. Mundubile however told the BBC that there was no militia at his home. "It's unfortunate that senior government officials would present themselves before the entire nation to make such falsehoods," he told BBC Focus on Africa. According to Kangwa, among those arrested were Patrick Mwansa, the husband of Tasila Lungu, the daughter of former Zambian President Edgar Lungu, and other politicians. The suspects are being held in custody at various police stations in Lusaka.

Mundubile described the raid to the BBC in detail, saying armed personnel knocked down the gate with an armoured vehicle, broke doors and windows and opened fire. "They were basically shooting indiscriminately. They directed two shots towards me. Like I've always said, it was just by God's grace that I survived. Mundubile said former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was shot while he and his wife were present. He said Kafwaya, whose whereabouts remain unknown, was bleeding and he urged the officers to take him to hospital. Mundubile said his family remains traumatised. "My children saw their uncle… bleeding profusely and being dragged like an animal… 80 soldiers coming into the house, shooting indiscriminately and breaking doors

payload.title: Sambiassa pidätettiin 11 ihmistä vaalien jälkeen – presidenttiehdokas kiistää kapinasyytökset
payload.summary: Sambian hallitus epäilee johtavia oppositiopoliitikkoja aseellisen kapinan suunnittelusta. Presidenttiehdokas Brian Mundubile kiistää syytökset ja väittää turvallisuusjoukkojen yrittäneen surmata hänet.
payload.content:
Sambian turvallisuusjoukot ovat pidättäneet 11 ihmistä vain päiviä torstaina järjestettyjen presidentinvaalien jälkeen. Hallituksen mukaan pidätettyihin kuuluu johtavia oppositiopoliitikkoja, joita epäillään aseellisen kapinan suunnittelusta. Opposition johtava presidenttiehdokas Brian Mundubile kiistää syytökset ja väittää perjantaina kotiinsa tehdyn ratsian olleen häneen kohdistunut murhayritys. Hallitus kertoo joukkojen myös takavarikoineen aseita.

## Hallitus vetoaa valtion turvallisuuteen

Sambian korkein virkamies Patrick Kangwa sanoi pidätettyjen liittyneen sotilaallisiin suunnitelmiin, joihin osallistui hänen mukaansa ulkomaalaisia, sekä laittomiin sotilaskoulutusleireihin. Kwangaan mukaan turvallisuusjoukot löysivät sotilasaseita, ammuksia ja muuta aseelliseen kapinaan tarkoitettua materiaalia. Hän kuvasi epäiltyjä vakavaksi uhaksi valtion turvallisuudelle.

Kangwa kertoi lisäksi, että viranomaisia kohti ammuttiin ratsian aikana, minkä jälkeen osapuolet vaihtoivat tulta. Mundubile löydettiin hänen mukaansa ratsian tapahtumapaikalta Lusakassa. Pidätettyjen joukossa on Kwangaan mukaan Patrick Mwansa, entisen presidentin Edgar Lungun tyttären Tasila Lungun aviomies, sekä muita poliitikkoja. Epäiltyjä pidetään pääkaupungin eri poliisiasemilla.

## Mundubile kiistää hallituksen väitteet

Mundubile sanoi BBC:n haastattelussa, ettei hänen kodissaan ollut miliisiä, ja kutsui hallituksen syytöksiä täysin sepitettyiksi. Hänen mukaansa aseistetut joukot kaatoivat portin panssaroidulla ajoneuvolla, rikkoivat ovia ja ikkunoita sekä ampuivat summittaisesti. Mundubile väittää, että kaksi laukausta suunnattiin suoraan häntä kohti. Hän arvioi kotiin tulleen noin 80 sotilasta ja sanoi perheensä järkyttyneen ratsiasta.

Mundubile sanoi olleensa vaimonsa kanssa paikalla, kun entistä ministeriä Mutotwe Kafwayaa ammuttiin. Hänen mukaansa Kafwaya vuoti runsaasti verta, ja hän pyysi turvallisuusjoukkoja viemään tämän sairaalaan. Kafwayan olinpaikka ei ollut tiedossa. Mundubile kertoi myös lastensa nähneen verta vuotavan sukulaisensa joutuvan raahatuksi. Hallituksen ja Mundubilen kuvaukset ratsian tapahtumista poikkeavat olennaisesti toisistaan.

## Ääntenlaskenta jatkuu

Ääntenlaskenta torstain vaaleista jatkuu. Kun tulokset oli julkistettu yli puolesta maan vaalipiireistä, istuva presidentti Hakainde Hichilema oli Mundubilen edellä. Mundubile oli jo aiemmin ilmoittanut voittaneensa vaalit ja väittänyt äänestyksessä tapahtuneen sääntöjenvastaisuuksia. Lopullista vaalitulosta ei ollut vielä vahvistettu.

Ääntenlaskenta jatkuu, ja Hakainde Hichilema oli julkistetuissa tuloksissa Mundubilen edellä.

article.journalist_note: Hallituksen ja opposition kuvaukset ratsian tapahtumista ovat ristiriidassa. Kiistanalaiset tiedot on attribuoitu, eikä kumpaakaan tapahtumakuvausta esitetä riippumattomasti vahvistettuna.
article.source_text:
The counting of votes from Thursday's poll is still going on Security forces in Zambia have seized weapons and arrested 11 people, including senior opposition figures, allegedly involved in an insurrection plot, the government has said. The leading opposition candidate in last Thursday's presidential election, Brian Mundubile, was also found at the scene of the raid in the capital, Lusaka, according to the country's top civil servant Patrick Kangwa. In an interview with the BBC, Mundubile dismissed the accusations as "total fabrications", saying security forces staged an assassination attempt on his life during a raid at his home on Friday. With results from more than half of the constituencies announced, he is trailing incumbent Hakainde Hichilema. Mundubile had earlier claimed victory and alleged there were voting irregularities.

The leading opposition candidate calls allegations of a planned insurrection as "total fabrications".

Giving details about the raid, Kangwa said the individuals arrested were connected to "military plans involving foreign nationals and illegal military training camps". He added that they posed "a serious threat to state security" and held "high-grade military weapons", ammunition and other materials intended for use in an armed insurrection. He alleged that shots were fired at law enforcement officers leading to an exchange of fire. Mundubile however told the BBC that there was no militia at his home. "It's unfortunate that senior government officials would present themselves before the entire nation to make such falsehoods," he told BBC Focus on Africa. According to Kangwa, among those arrested were Patrick Mwansa, the husband of Tasila Lungu, the daughter of former Zambian President Edgar Lungu, and other politicians. The suspects are being held in custody at various police stations in Lusaka.

Mundubile described the raid to the BBC in detail, saying armed personnel knocked down the gate with an armoured vehicle, broke doors and windows and opened fire. "They were basically shooting indiscriminately. They directed two shots towards me. Like I've always said, it was just by God's grace that I survived. Mundubile said former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was shot while he and his wife were present. He said Kafwaya, whose whereabouts remain unknown, was bleeding and he urged the officers to take him to hospital. Mundubile said his family remains traumatised.
